scenarios.answer: The site conforms to WCAG version 2.2 at level AA.

proposed.rationale: The answer explicitly claims the named minimum standard.

scenarios.answer: We chose high contrast colours for the homepage.

proposed.rationale: Colour choices alone do not address the full WCAG standard.

scenarios.answer: We tried VoiceOver on one page; the remaining screen-reader journeys have not been checked.

proposed.rationale: Trying one assistive technology does not show the service works across common tools.

scenarios.answer: The service currently cannot be operated using a screen reader.

evidence.quote: cannot be operated using a screen reader

proposed.rationale: The answer explicitly denies one important assistive-technology capability.

scenarios.answer: Participants with disabilities joined our user interviews.

evidence.quote: Participants with disabilities joined our user interviews.

proposed.rationale: Equivalent claim of disabled participation, without verifying research records.

scenarios.answer: We interviewed customers about the login screen.

proposed.rationale: The statement does not say whether disabled people participated.

scenarios.answer: Our accessibility statement will be drafted after the public-beta launch.

evidence.quote: will be drafted after the public-beta launch

proposed.rationale: The promised timing is later than the specified publication milestone.

scenarios.answer: We plan to publish an accessibility statement when the service enters public beta.

proposed.rationale: Future intention alone does not establish actual publication or completeness.

scenarios.answer: No money has been allocated to accessibility work.

evidence.quote: No money has been allocated to accessibility work.

proposed.rationale: Budgeting guidance is explicitly unfulfilled in the stated plan.

scenarios.answer: Our delivery budget includes time for accessibility training and testing.

evidence.quote: budget includes time for accessibility training and testing

proposed.rationale: The plan explicitly includes accessibility costs, not proof the funds exist.

scenarios.answer: We did not hire an external auditor; our internal accessibility audit status has not been reported.

proposed.rationale: Not hiring an external specialist does not rule out an internal audit.

scenarios.answer: A trained internal specialist completed the pre-beta accessibility audit.

evidence.quote: A trained internal specialist completed the pre-beta accessibility audit.

proposed.rationale: The claim is an acceptable route to obtaining an audit, but no proof was supplied.

scenarios.answer: No accessibility audit has been performed before public beta.

evidence.quote: No accessibility audit has been performed before public beta.

proposed.rationale: The answer denies an audit of any kind within the required period.

scenarios.answer: Our team ran automated accessibility checks.

proposed.rationale: Automated checks are not the stated accessibility audit.

scenarios.answer: We published an accessibility statement on the website.

proposed.rationale: Publication does not address disclosure of specific accessibility issues.

scenarios.answer: Every page footer includes a link to the accessibility statement.

evidence.quote: Every page footer includes a link to the accessibility statement.

proposed.rationale: The answer claims that the statement is accessible from every page.

scenarios.answer: We do not publish a mobile application; this is a desktop browser service.

proposed.rationale: The mobile-app-specific clause may be inapplicable; absence is not evidence of breach.

scenarios.answer: The accessibility statement is reviewed every January.

proposed.rationale: The claimed annual schedule would meet the recommended frequency.

scenarios.answer: We send postal letters but only provide standard-print versions when accessible formats are requested.

proposed.rationale: The service says it sends letters yet refuses requested accessible formats.

scenarios.answer: We aim to arrange an accessibility audit after launch.

proposed.rationale: Planning after launch conflicts with advice to plan during alpha.

scenarios.answer: We tested with disabled volunteers; whether older users were included is not recorded.

proposed.rationale: The older-user aspect is not established, even if disability testing is claimed.

scenarios.answer: The Service Standard applies, but we did not test with any older users.

evidence.quote: did not test with any older users

proposed.rationale: The stated standard applies and an explicit required participant group was omitted.

scenarios.answer: Our team tests each new feature before beta, but stops accessibility tests once public beta begins.

evidence.quote: stops accessibility tests once public beta begins

proposed.rationale: The answer explicitly excludes the required public-beta testing period.

scenarios.answer: We have an automated accessibility-test suite.

proposed.rationale: Having a suite does not establish running it after every public-beta feature.

scenarios.answer: All tests are automated; we do no manual accessibility testing.

evidence.quote: we do no manual accessibility testing

proposed.rationale: The answer explicitly rules out one required approach.

scenarios.answer: We run manual accessibility reviews alongside automated scans every sprint.

evidence.quote: manual accessibility reviews alongside automated scans every sprint

proposed.rationale: The claim mentions both modalities and recurring cadence.

scenarios.answer: We checked Chrome on one desktop; compatibility with other browsers and mobile devices is unknown.

proposed.rationale: Checking one browser cannot demonstrate broad compatibility, and non-support is not proven.

scenarios.answer: We support mainstream browsers across desktop and mobile devices.

evidence.quote: support mainstream browsers across desktop and mobile devices

proposed.rationale: The answer asserts browser and device coverage, without testing evidence.

scenarios.answer: An audit was completed, but critical issues remain unfixed before public beta.

evidence.quote: critical issues remain unfixed before public beta

proposed.rationale: A finished audit alone does not satisfy the additional remediation obligation.

scenarios.answer: The accessibility audit is scheduled and the remediation plan is being drafted.

proposed.rationale: It is not established whether both audit and fixes will be completed before public beta.

scenarios.answer: We are not claiming compliance with the Service Standard.

proposed.rationale: The conditional source obligation may not apply in this scenario.

scenarios.answer: The product meets WCAG 2.2 level AA, according to our team.

proposed.rationale: Claimed conformance is present but no audit was inspected.

scenarios.answer: We ran automated accessibility checks, but have not assessed operation with assistive technologies.

proposed.rationale: Automated scans don't establish working with common assistive technologies.

scenarios.answer: We recruited participants through our own user panel.

proposed.rationale: An external recruitment agency is only an example of an optional expense.

scenarios.answer: Research participants joined remotely without paid taxis.

proposed.rationale: A taxi expense is not itself mandatory for every research session.
Same WCAG 2.2 AA conformance baseline from two pages.
Both require operation with common assistive technologies.
The testing guide adds fixing audit issues, which is not entailed by obtaining an audit.
Publishing a statement and making it available from every page are different dimensions.
Disabled participants in research does not entail testing disabled AND older users.
Per-feature beta cadence and manual+automated recurring modalities are different obligations.
Budget allocation and alpha-stage audit planning are different planning criteria.
WCAG AA conformance and assistive-technology operation cannot be substituted.
Every-page statement discovery and mobile-app alternative placements have different applicability.
Browser/device support is distinct from assistive-technology functionality.
Same underlying pre-beta accessibility-audit requirement.
Identical automated-plus-manual recurring testing criterion.
Publishing a statement need not include a description of issues unless contents also addressed.
Audit-and-fix cannot be merged into only-audit, regardless of ordering.
Same disabled-user research requirement.
Service Standard's general conditional requirements and specific user-testing obligation are not equivalent.
Different illustrative costs are neither obligatory nor equivalent.
